definition: The ritual bathing of a deity, most often a Shivling, with water, milk or other prescribed substances.
The spoken vow of intent taken before a ritual, naming who performs it and why.
A lunar day, one-thirtieth of the lunar month; the unit that dates every vrat and festival.
A lunar fortnight: Shukla (waxing) or Krishna (waning) half of the month.
One of 27 lunar mansions the Moon crosses in a month, used for ritual timing.
A vowed observance, typically a fast joined to worship on a fixed tithi.
The materials a ritual calls for — from jal and bilva to diya and dhoop.
The bael tree and its trifoliate leaf, the offering most dear to Shiva.
The formal breaking of a fast in its prescribed window, completing the vrat.
An auspicious window of time computed from the panchang for beginning an act.
A daily period traditionally avoided for new beginnings; its length shifts with sunrise and sunset.
Food offered to the deity and returned as blessing, shared after the puja.
The closing act of worship — circling a lit lamp before the deity with song.
Repetition of a mantra a counted number of times, commonly 11, 21, 51 or 108.
The monsoon month sacred to Shiva; its Mondays carry the Sawan Somwar vrat.
The eleventh tithi of each paksha, observed as a Vishnu fast twice a month.
A lamp kept continuously lit through an observance, most often across the nine nights of Navratri. Relight it if it goes out; nothing is void.
Unbroken rice grains, usually mixed with a little turmeric or kumkum. Offered in almost every puja. The point is that the grains are whole.
The four monsoon months from Devshayani to Devutthana Ekadashi. Weddings and some new undertakings are traditionally deferred through this period.
What is offered to a purohit after a ritual. Traditionally given according to means and not fixed as a fee.
The installation of the kalash on the first day of Navratri, performed in the morning while Pratipada prevails and before Hindu midday.
A brass or copper pot filled with water, topped with mango leaves and a coconut. It stands for the presence invited into the space.
Five ingredients mixed for abhishek and prasad — milk, curd, ghee, honey and sugar. Made fresh, distributed after.
A period before and during an eclipse in which some activities are set aside. It applies only where the eclipse is actually visible.
